newsitem.title: USA: Juror is dismissed in secondhand smoke trial.
newsitem.headline: Juror is dismissed in secondhand smoke trial.

text.p: A 43-year-old woman described by court staff as disruptive was dropped on Friday from the six-member jury scheduled to hear a $5 billion secondhand-smoke trial beginning on Monday.
A court official said Dade County Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye made the decision to excuse the juror, one of two smokers among the original six jurors, in a private meeting with lawyers.
One of eight alternate jurors will replace the dropped juror, the official said.
Details about the replacement juror were not immediately available.

A court bailiff on Thursday told the judge in court that the dismissed juror, a hospital accounts worker, had repeatedly complained to court staff about payments due her for jury duty and other matters and was likely to continue to be disruptive during a trial expected to last at least eight weeks.
The judge made no comment on the jury when pre-trial hearings resumed this morning.
A six-person jury and 10 alternates were chosen on Wednesday after nearly six weeks of painstaking questioning of hundreds of potential jurors. Two altnerate jurors were dismissed yesterday.
In the case, flight attendants are suing tobacco companies, alleging they were sickened by secondhand smoke in airliners.
